change: Host verifier selection is saved in the protected contract journal and chosen before decoding. Unknown keys and ambiguous unselected formats fail without fallback.

Contract values retain original canonical data and method observations, not executable implementations. Journal replay uses original proposals rather than inferring a registration from the contract format.
Dispatch rebinds exact canonical data, description, method/configuration/schema and checker identity through the installed host registry. File authority is not derived from changed binding metadata.

The existing kernel checker field binds definition identity plus native recipe. Completion derives that value from the actual validated report, retaining the unchanged consuming controller and input-bound evidence path.
Same-byte method switches/upgrades create a new obligation and host-review revision. Rejection preserves accepted meaning; no grant/job/evidence is restored on restart.

Old journal entries without original method metadata retain exact accepted data and obligations as unknown history. A fresh reviewed proposal recovers checking; missing new-format binding metadata is refused. No current method is stamped onto old records.
TUI resolves only host-owned selection before preparing tools, opens the workspace afterward, and rechecks the selection before starting. Flagless finite resume does not prepare Lean.

Unknown saved/explicit selection preserves the journal; unavailable and upgraded original methods retain old metadata without execution
Missing historical method data stays unknown and recovers through a new review; stripped bindings and changed source metadata cannot supply file authority
